Adjusting for that search — and for this run's own sample size (2924 days), skew, and kurtosis — there is an estimated 17% probability that this strategy's true long-run Sharpe ratio exceeds 0.19, the Sharpe you'd expect from the best of 21 equally-skilled, zero-edge trials by chance alone. (Before accounting for the number of trials searched, PSR-vs-zero was 37%.) This is not a p-value or a guarantee — it is the model's best point estimate of the strategy's true statistical edge, not a certainty.
